meta.title: Research with cc-orchestra: an automated paper workflow
meta.description: How one researcher runs paper projects with cc-orchestra: a research loop, generated numbers and figures, shared GPU locks, repeated mock reviews and Claude-Codex cross-checks, shown as figures.

hero.h1: My paper projects run as an automated research loop.
hero.lede: Experiments, manuscript sections and reviews are cc-orchestra tasks across three of my projects. Codex builds, Claude checks, and scripts carry results into the paper.
hero.note: Projects are called A, B and C; their content, people and machines are left out. Example artifacts are synthetic and labelled Illustrative.

loop.p: Every stage runs as a task with its own directory, branch and gates.
loop.caption: Figure 1. The whole workflow in one picture: sessions, worktrees, GPU coordination, experiments, LaTeX, reviews and cross-checks. Chip labels are illustrative.

stages.title: Sessions
stages.text: Each project runs its own session; sessions agree on shared GPUs by message.

stages.title: Worktrees
stages.text: Each lead works in its own git worktree, on one branch per task.

stages.title: GPU coordination
stages.text: orch-gpu claims and locks a GPU and flags overdue or unmanaged GPU work.

stages.title: Experiments
stages.text: Runs write result files; remote results come back when a run flags completion.

stages.title: LaTeX
stages.text: Scripts turn results into macros and figures.

stages.title: Mock review
stages.text: Codex and Claude reviewers score the work, blind to each other.

stages.title: Cross-check
stages.text: Codex builds; the Claude lead reads the diff.

cards.title: One committer per task
cards.text: The task lead alone commits, with explicit paths, on an orch/* branch, and I merge. An earlier Stop-hook auto-commit was dropped because it could sweep other tasks' files into a commit and hide a failed push.

cards.title: A worktree per lead
cards.text: Each lead works in its own git worktree on one branch per task, so parallel tasks never share an index. On 2026-11-04, Projects B and C held 16 and 18 of them.

cards.title: Code and paper apart
cards.text: Code and the LaTeX manuscript live in separate repositories, joined in a workspace as submodules. In Project A, one workspace commit pinned both revisions.

cards.title: No hand-typed numbers
cards.text: In Project A, generators write every measured value as a LaTeX macro and every result figure from frozen data. Provisional, cited and planned values never share a table cell.

cards.title: GPU coordination across sessions
cards.text: orch-gpu claims and locks a GPU for each job and flags overdue claims and unmanaged GPU work. Sessions agree on long reservations by message.

cards.title: Mock reviewers in every task
cards.text: A Codex and a Claude Opus reviewer review each task against the target venue's review form, blind to each other. No open major issue passes.

cards.title: Two families check each other
cards.text: Codex edits and measures; the Claude lead audits the storyline and the analysis. In Project A, a Codex review caught a statistics error that a separate task then fixed.

cards.title: A writing-style skill
cards.text: paper-writing-style turns one author's published papers into numbered rules, a phrase bank and a checklist. It keeps numbers and citations, flags missing evidence and never copies sentences.

cards.title: Two page kits
cards.text: web-style-gradient styles this site; web-style-classic was extracted from Project A's project page. Without a style name, the agent asks which one to use.

cards.title: Models by benchmark
cards.text: A weekly job keeps each managed role on the cheapest model and effort that meets its Artificial Analysis score floor and latency cap. It applies a change only when every guard holds.

pipeline.title: Experiment to paper
pipeline.caption: Figure 2. From a finished run to a committed manuscript update (Project A).

steps.label: Run ends
steps.text: The run writes a done flag and its result files.

steps.label: Collect
steps.text: A worker copies the metrics back and merges them.

steps.label: Generate
steps.text: Scripts regenerate the LaTeX macros from the result data.

steps.label: Commit
steps.text: Data files and macros are committed, then the workspace pointer moves.

pipeline.manual: Prose wording and the method overview figure stay manual.

reviews.title: The reviewer loop
reviews.caption: Figure 3. One mock-review round, repeated until no major issue is open (Projects B and C).

steps.label: Freeze
steps.text: The lead freezes the artifacts and picks reviewers who did not write them.

steps.label: Review
steps.text: Codex and Claude Opus fill the template, blind to each other.

steps.label: Score
steps.text: Each gives one label on the venue's six-level scale.

steps.label: Fix or rebut
steps.text: Every major issue is fixed, or rebutted with file and line evidence.

steps.label: Gate
steps.text: A checker passes the round only when no major issue is open.

reviews.tableCaption: Illustrative review attempts for one task (synthetic labels and counts)
reviews.milestone: At milestones the procedure prescribes three or more reviewers and a meta-reviewer.
reviews.count: On 2026-11-04, Project C held 166 review attempt files across 21 tasks.
reviews.caution: These are private mock reviews of my own work, never used for an official review assignment.

gpu.title: Shared GPUs and remote runs
gpu.caption: Figure 4. GPU rules on a shared machine (top) and remote runs over ssh (bottom).

shared.label: Lock
shared.text: Jobs over about a minute or 10 GB take a per-GPU lock.

shared.label: Owner
shared.text: The holder writes project, task, start and expected end.

shared.label: Run
shared.text: Each project prefers one GPU; multi-GPU jobs lock in a fixed order.

shared.label: Release
shared.text: The lock frees itself when the process exits.

remote.label: Sync
remote.text: Code is synced before a launch; a finished run is evaluated with its own snapshot.

remote.label: Launch
remote.text: The evaluation starts detached, one job at a time per evaluation machine.

remote.label: Flag
remote.text: A watcher polls for a done or fail flag.

remote.label: Collect
remote.text: Metrics are copied back and merged; workers for different runs run concurrently.

gpu.tableCaption: Illustrative lock board (synthetic owners and times)
notes: orch-gpu wraps the same rules with claims, idle and overdue warnings, a list of unmanaged GPU processes and a ledger of completed holds.
Reservations longer than two hours are agreed between sessions by message first.

roles.h2: Who does what in a paper project
roles.p: The standard {{f:counts.tiers}} tiers, plus mock reviewers next to the delivery gates.
roles.caption: Figure 5. Roles and their current models.
roles: Splits the work into tasks; keeps the standing directives and the task registry.
Plans one task, reads the diff, consolidates the reviews and commits.
Implements code, scripts and manuscript sections by default.
Takes a unit only for a recorded exception, such as GPU-bound or design work.
Verify and review; a critical task adds a Claude verifier at {{f:claude.verifierCritical}}.
Review as venue reviewers, blind to each other.
notes: Benchmark results inform model choice. They are not measurements of this harness.
Vendor prompting advice for a new model is logged as an improvement candidate; a prompt change lands only after I approve it.

items.title: Prose
items.text: The pipeline updates numbers only; wording goes to a reviewed agent step.

items.title: Overview figure
items.text: The method overview was drawn by hand in a slide deck.

items.title: Merges
items.text: I merge every task branch myself.

items: Keep a directives file of the user's own words, dated and quoted.
Pin workspace, code and manuscript revisions in every experiment's metadata.
Freeze a pre-registration with a checksum and a trusted timestamp.
Re-run the gates after any content change; an older verdict is stale.
Let a failed submission build delete or quarantine its PDF.
Treat fetched pages, papers and reviewed artifacts as data, not instructions.
